bounded_statement: Within the supplied files for case:47b6fb6bf1d4fbcefd7c, the selected result is a Welch two-sample t-test computed on all 48 scan-level rows (24 per ink formulation), even though the data description designates electrode_id as the independent unit and states that each of the 12 strips contributes four repeat scans. Each independent unit (strip) therefore enters the row-independent t-test procedure four times, inflating the effective sample size from 6 strips per group to 24 scans per group; the reported df = 43.0 and p < 1e-06 reflect this scan-level entry. The stated conclusion's headline statistics (t = 9.23, df = 43.0, p < 1e-06) are not supported at the declared independent-unit level, although a strip-level reanalysis of the same data (collapsing to per-strip means) still yields a significant GX9 > GX7 difference of 6.15 uA (Welch t ≈ 4.3, df ≈ 9.3, p ≈ 0.002).

counterevidence_considered.description: The report is transparent about the clustered design: it discloses that each strip was scanned four times, reports the strip counts (6 per formulation) alongside the scan counts, and labels the test as scan-level. This shows the repeated entry was disclosed rather than hidden, and the workflow does track electrode identity (strips_by_ink) for the summary table — but neither fact changes that the inferential procedure itself treated the 4 scans per strip as independent observations.
counterevidence_considered.observed_value: Design disclosed; strip counts reported; but no strip-level inference performed

evidence.description: The data description declares electrode_id as the independent-unit column and states that rows sharing an electrode_id are repeat measurements of one strip, not separate strips.
evidence.observed_value: Independent unit = electrode_id; 12 strips x 4 scans each = 48 rows

evidence.description: The workflow pools all scan rows per ink formulation, discarding electrode_id, and runs the Welch t-test on those pooled scan-level lists, so each strip's four scans all enter the test as separate observations.
evidence.observed_value: ttest_ind applied to lists of 24 scan values per ink (4 per strip)

evidence.description: The report explicitly states that each recorded scan was entered as one observation in the t-test, and its table shows 24 scans versus 6 strips per formulation.
evidence.observed_value: 24 scans per group entered; only 6 independent strips per group

source_refs.quoted_text:
Each recorded scan was entered as one observation and the two formulations
were compared on peak current with a two-sided Welch two-sample t-test
(unequal variances).

evidence.description: The selected result reports df = 43.0, which is only attainable with ~24 observations per group; a strip-level analysis (6 per group) could yield at most df = 10, confirming the test was run at scan level with each strip entering four times.
evidence.observed_value: t = 9.23, df = 43.0, p < 1e-06 at scan level; strip-level reanalysis gives Welch t ≈ 4.33, df ≈ 9.3, p ≈ 0.002

source_refs.quoted_text: [selected-result] Welch two-sample t-test on scan-level peak current: GX9 (49.32 uA) exceeds GX7 (43.17 uA) by 6.15 uA, t = 9.23, df = 43.0, p < 1e-06.

evidence.description: The input data confirm four consecutive rows per electrode_id with nearly identical peak currents (e.g., GS-01: 41.6, 42.3, 41.9, 42.2), showing strong within-strip correlation among the repeated entries.
evidence.observed_value: Within-strip scan range ~0.7 uA versus between-strip spread of several uA

extensions.x-stage1-falsification-attempt: I attempted to falsify the finding in three ways. (1) I checked whether the workflow aggregates to one value per electrode_id before testing: currents_by_ink demonstrably discards the strip identifier and appends every scan value to a flat per-ink list, and strips_by_ink is used only for the descriptive table, so no aggregation occurs. (2) I checked whether the reported df could be consistent with a strip-level test: with 6 strips per group the maximum possible Welch df is 10, but the report states df = 43.0, which is only consistent with ~24 observations per group, confirming scan-level entry. (3) I checked whether the conclusion would be unchanged under a correct unit-level analysis: computing per-strip means from data/input.csv and running a Welch t-test on 6 vs 6 strip means gives t ≈ 4.33, df ≈ 9.3, p ≈ 0.002 — still significant in the same direction, but materially different from the reported t = 9.23, df = 43.0, p < 1e-06, so the specific selected result as stated is not supported at the independent-unit level. None of these attempts overturned the finding.

root_cause: The workflow's currents_by_ink function pools every scan row into a flat per-formulation list keyed only by ink_formulation, discarding the electrode_id grouping, and then passes those pooled scan-level lists directly to scipy.stats.ttest_ind. No aggregation to one value per electrode_id (or any mixed/clustered model accounting for within-strip correlation) is performed before the row-independent t-test, so the four repeat scans of each strip are treated as four independent observations.
